prompt: In a circle of radius $9$, an arc has length $6\pi$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the arc's central angle?
hint: Compare the arc with the whole circumference. The fraction of the circumference equals the fraction of a full turn.

hints.text: Compare the arc with the whole circumference. The fraction of the circumference equals the fraction of a full turn.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a half circle: radius $2$ gives circumference $4\pi$, so an arc of $2\pi$ is half the circle, or $180°$. Find the fraction, then take that fraction of $360°$.
The circumference is $2\pi(9) = 18\pi$, so the arc is $\dfrac{6\pi}{18\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ of the circle. Take that fraction of $360°$.
One third of $360°$ is $120°$, so the central angle measures $120$ degrees.

learningObjective: Recover a central angle from an arc length.
explanation: The full circumference of the circle is $2\pi r = 2\pi(9) = 18\pi$.
The arc is $\dfrac{6\pi}{18\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ of the circumference, so its angle is one third of a full turn.
One third of $360°$ is $120°$, so the central angle measures $120$ degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: Or use s = rθ and convert
steps: In radians, arc length is radius times angle, so $6\pi = 9\theta$ and $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
Convert to degrees by multiplying by $\dfrac{180}{\pi}$, which cancels the $\pi$.
The result is $\dfrac{2 \times 180}{3} = 120$, so the central angle is $120$ degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Stopping at $\dfrac{2\pi}{3} \approx 2.09$ gives the angle in radians, but the question asks for degrees.
The arc is $\dfrac{6\pi}{18\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ of the circumference, so the angle is one third of a full turn.
One third of $360$ degrees is $120$ degrees.
